review: The hymn is the night-watch of the bride: 1:1–4 is Isa 21:11–12 (שֹׁמֵר מַה־מִּלַּיְלָה) with Ps 130:6, 2:1–4 is Ps 130:6 (מִשֹּׁמְרִים לַבֹּקֶר) nearly verbatim, 3:1–4 is Rev 22:17 with Matt 13:45–46 (the pearl), 4:1–4 is Rev 22:20 with Song 5:2 (קוֹל דּוֹדִי דוֹפֵק), 5:1–4 is Ps 121:4 (לֹא־יָנוּם שֹׁמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל), and 6:1–4 is 2 Pet 1:19 (כְּנֵר מֵאִיר בַּמָּקוֹם הַחֹשֶׁךְ) with Rev 22:16.

1:3 and 2:3–4 lean on Ps 130:6 twice; the Hebrew repeats the psalm's watchmen phrase (שֹׁמְרֵי בֹקֶר) in both places, because the print repeats the Arabic رَاقِبُ الصَّبَاح and the repetition is the stanza's clock.

3:3–4 תִּזְרַח כְּפִנִּינָה … כְּאֶבֶן הַיְקָר — the Arabic لُؤْلُؤَةً … كَأَكْرَمِ حَجَرِ يَشْب keeps two separate images (a pearl, and a glowing costly stone); the Hebrew keeps both with פְּנִינִים (Job 28:18) and אֶבֶן יְקָרָה, rather than merging them into one jewel.

5:3–4 וְאִם כָּאן עֵינֵינוּ שׁוֹקְדוֹת לָךְ / גַּם־אַתָּה שׁוֹקֵד לָנוּ — the Arabic فَأَنْتَ كَذَا سَاهِر uses the same watching root for God; the Hebrew uses שָׁקַד for both halves (Jer 1:12, שֹׁקֵד אֲנִי עַל־דְּבָרִי), so the line says that His watching answers ours in kind.
